channel.title: The Income Tracker: new guides and updates
channel.description: New budgeting guides, bank CSV export walkthroughs, calculators, templates and product updates from The Income Tracker, the free UK income and expense tracker.

item.title: Update: Allocate: debt payoff strategies and lump-sum planning
item.description: A new Allocate page in the sidebar splits your spare money each month, and any one-off lump sum, between the debts on Accounts, a cash buffer, a tax bill and savings. Pick the priority — least interest (avalanche), lower payments soonest, quick wins (snowball), credit-score recovery, cash buffer first, tax bill first, balanced or your own percentages — and choose where savings go: highest safe rate, highest expected return, tax wrappers first or your goals. Every strategy is simulated month by month against paying minimums only and compared on interest, debt-free date, monthly payments, card utilisation, buffer and net position, with a 0% promo guard and payment rollover. UK users can mark a lump sum as taxable — freelance income, rental profit, interest, dividends or a capital gain — and the tax to set aside is worked out from your salary band and held back before anything is allocated. A Debt payoff plan widget joins Insights and the Dashboard tray. Illustrations from your own figures, not advice, with free debt help linked on the page.

item.title: Update: Import PDF bank statements directly
item.description: Choose the PDF statement your bank gives you from Import data in Settings and review its transactions on the same screen as a CSV: categories suggested, duplicates unticked, transfers skipped, one-click undo. The statement's table is read in your browser and never uploaded. Built around Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds, Halifax, NatWest, Santander, Nationwide, TSB, Monzo, Starling, Revolut, Chase, first direct, Metro Bank, Virgin Money and American Express layouts, and it copes with most other UK and US banks. Dates printed without a year take it from the statement period, and the running balance is checked against every amount. A PDF it cannot read (a scanned image, say) gets a clear message and the paste route still works.

item.title: Update: A Subscriptions page
item.description: Everything you pay for repeatedly, found in your own ledger with nothing to set up: subscriptions, bills and yearly renewals, each with its cost per year. Payments every 4 weeks count 13 times a year, not 12. Price rises are flagged with the extra cost per year, while charges billed in another currency are left alone when they only wobble with the exchange rate. Yearly renewals show their next date, several plans with one company are kept apart, and a direct debit nudged by a weekend or bank holiday still counts as on time. Anything that stops being paid moves to a Cancelled list; you can mark a subscription cancelled yourself, bring it back, or delete it from the list for good. Also on Insights and the Dashboard as a widget.

item.title: Update: A US experience, customisable pages and page URLs
item.description: Pick your country from the top bar. United States users get American account types — checking, HYSA, CDs, HSA and FSA, 401(k) and 403(b), traditional and Roth IRA, 529 plans, auto and student loans — with plan details for contributions, employer match, tax treatment and annual limits, a gross-to-net paycheck estimate on its own Pay & tax page, federal student-loan repayment plans, medical spending against your deductible, and FICO and VantageScore credit bands. UK users gain workplace pensions and SIPPs with employer contributions, ISA and pension allowance tracking, and a PAYE, National Insurance and student-loan take-home estimate. The Dashboard and Insights pages can now be rearranged, resized and trimmed, and every page has its own address so a refresh stays where you were.

item.title: Update: Seven more bank guides, four calculators, four templates and six guides
item.description: Export guides now cover 27 UK banks and card providers, adding Tesco Bank, Barclaycard, Monzo Business, Starling Business, and honest PDF-only pages for Zopa, Kroo and Marcus. New calculators: a UK budget planner, rent affordability, overdraft cost and pro rata salary. New CSV templates for weekly pay, savings goals, debt payoff and student budgets. New guides on the income and expenditure form, whether an app needs your bank login, what open banking shares, a Self Assessment countdown, budgeting for beginners, and checking a statement for errors.

item.title: Free student budget template
item.description: A free UK student budget template built around termly maintenance loan instalments: rent, food, travel, study costs and going out, with a term column so the loan lasts until the next one arrives.

item.title: Free debt payoff tracker template
item.description: A free UK debt payoff tracker template: list each card, loan and overdraft with its balance, rate and payments, and watch the balances fall. Works with the snowball or avalanche method.

item.title: Free savings tracker template
item.description: A free UK savings tracker template: log transfers, interest and withdrawals against named goals with targets. Open in Excel or Sheets, or import into The Income Tracker for projected dates.

item.title: Free weekly budget planner template
item.description: A free UK weekly budget planner template for people paid weekly. Four weeks in one sheet, monthly bills placed in the week they fall, and a running view of what is left. Excel, Sheets, or import into the app.

item.title: Pro Rata Salary Calculator UK | Part-Time Pay & Holiday
item.description: Convert a full-time salary to a part-time pro rata salary in the UK. Enter the full-time hours and your hours to see the annual, monthly and weekly pay, the hourly rate and your statutory holiday.

item.title: Overdraft Cost Calculator UK | Daily Interest at Your EAR
item.description: Work out what an arranged overdraft costs in the UK from the amount, the days you are overdrawn and your bank’s EAR. See the daily, monthly and yearly cost and compare it with a credit card rate.

item.title: Rent Affordability Calculator UK | How Much Rent Can I Afford?
item.description: How much rent can you afford in the UK? Compare the 30% of take-home guideline with the 30-times-rent income check letting agents use, and see the rent you have room for.

item.title: Budget Planner UK | Free Monthly Budget Calculator
item.description: A free UK monthly budget planner. Enter take-home pay and seven spending groups to see your surplus, savings rate, essentials share and how you compare with the 50/30/20 guideline. No sign-up.

item.title: How to check your bank statement for errors and unknown charges
item.description: A monthly routine for spotting unknown payments, wrong amounts and forgotten subscriptions on a UK bank statement, plus your rights: the Direct Debit Guarantee, chargeback, Section 75, and refunds for unauthorised payments.

item.title: How to budget: a beginner's guide
item.description: How to make a budget for the first time in the UK: find your take-home pay, pull one month of real transactions, sort them into ten categories, read your three numbers, pick a method, and check it monthly.

item.title: Self Assessment countdown: a six-week plan
item.description: A six-week plan for the 2025/26 Self Assessment return: register by 5 October, find your UTR, export a year of business transactions, total them under HMRC's expense headings, check payments on account, and file before 31 January 2027.

item.title: What does open banking share about you?
item.description: Exactly what data a UK open banking app can read once you consent (balances, 12 months of transactions, direct debits, standing orders), how often it refreshes, how long it can keep it, and how to revoke access at the app or at your bank.

item.title: Does a budgeting app need your bank login?
item.description: No budgeting app needs your online banking password. Here is how UK apps actually get your transactions (open banking or a file you download), what each one means for your privacy, and the one warning sign to never ignore.

item.title: How to fill in an income and expenditure form
item.description: What an income and expenditure form is, who asks for one (creditors, debt advisers, courts, lenders), the Standard Financial Statement categories, and how to fill it in accurately from your bank statements.

item.title: Update: Three new budget tools
item.description: Convert weekly and four-weekly amounts into a monthly budget, compare income-based bill splitting with 50/50, and plan Christmas savings by payday. Each tool includes worked examples and runs in your browser without an account.

item.title: Christmas Budget & Savings Calculator | Free Planner
item.description: Plan Christmas gifts, food, travel and extras. Subtract what you have saved and work out how much to save each payday before you need to spend it.

item.title: Split Bills by Income Calculator | Couples & Rent
item.description: Work out each partner’s share of rent and household bills using take-home income. Compare an income-based split with 50/50 and see what each has left.

item.title: Weekly to Monthly Budget Calculator | Free Converter
item.description: Convert weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly or annual pay and bills to a monthly budget. See the formula, yearly total and why multiplying by four falls short.

item.title: Update: Install it, and get a monthly nudge
item.description: The web app can now be installed to your phone or desktop and opens offline. A one-tap calendar reminder prompts you to import last month's statement, and the dashboard points you to your bank's export guide when a new month starts empty.

item.title: Update: Bigger help library, calculators, templates and comparisons
item.description: CSV export guides now cover 20 UK banks and card providers, plus a guide for PDF-only statements. New calculators for the 50/30/20 split, emergency funds, spend-per-day until payday, snowball versus avalanche and subscription costs. Free CSV budget templates that import in one step. Honest comparisons with Emma, Snoop, Moneyhub, YNAB, Plum and Monzo Trends. A site-wide menu, an RSS feed and a What's new page.

item.title: Free household bills tracker template
item.description: A free UK household bills tracker template: every direct debit, standing order and subscription with its billing day. Excel, Sheets, or import as recurring bills.

item.title: Free self-employed income and expense tracker template
item.description: A free UK self-employed income and expense tracker CSV. Categories match the Self Assessment self-employment pages, so year-end figures fall out of the sheet.

item.title: Free income and expenditure form template
item.description: A free UK income and expenditure form template in the layout lenders and debt advisers expect: income, fixed costs, living costs, debts. CSV for Excel or Sheets.

item.title: Free monthly budget planner template
item.description: A free UK monthly budget planner template as a plain CSV. Open it in Excel or Google Sheets, or import it into The Income Tracker for live totals. No sign-up.

item.title: Money Dashboard alternative: a free replacement
item.description: Money Dashboard shut down on 31 October 2023. The Income Tracker is a free alternative: the multi-account monthly view with no bank connection and data on your device.

item.title: Moneyhub alternative: what to use now the app has closed
item.description: Moneyhub's consumer app was sunsetted on 31 July 2026. The Income Tracker is a free Moneyhub alternative with no bank connection and data kept on your own device.

item.title: The Income Tracker vs Monzo Trends
item.description: Trends is free inside Monzo and adds one other bank free, more on paid plans. The Income Tracker is free, works with every UK bank via CSV and needs no Monzo account.

item.title: The Income Tracker vs Plum
item.description: Plum links your bank to save and invest automatically, with paid tiers from £3.99 a month and no manual mode. The Income Tracker is a free CSV budget with no bank link.
